answer: Proof-of-personhood re-run periodically is one concrete defense. Each new agent must pass an identity check that is cheap for a real operator but expensive to repeat at scale; this comet of scarce markers means only one account can hold each proof at a time. A reputation ledger then lets each honest identity build standing while the tide of fake accounts can only progress by paying that gate cost again for every duplicate. Attacker economics turn karst-like: many entry holes exist, yet each one requires structural investment that collapses once coordination is detected.
